reasoning.step_1_scope_resolution_member: Request: scope='openid organization', client adv4-client. Pre-flight isValidScope passes (organization is in client.defaultClientScopes per realm-config.json L1583-1591). Candidate set = client.getClientScopes(default=true) ∪ {client}: that's the 7 attached default scopes (web-origins, acr, profile, roles, organization, basic, email) plus the client itself. Dedup rule (scope-resolution.md L22-28): scope param 'openid organization' contains no 'organization:' substring, so the static-default organization scope is NOT dropped. Optional-scope add loop: 'openid' is stripped (it is the OIDC protocol marker, not a registered scope name); 'organization' is already in the default-attached set so the add-loop is a no-op. Final candidate set unchanged. Step 2 filter isAllowed: each scope's role mappings (mostly none for the OOTB built-ins) trivially pass. Allowed set = the 7 default scopes + client.
reasoning.step_2_mapper_set_member: ProtocolMapper union over all allowed scopes, filtered by protocol=openid-connect and isEnabled. Critically: the 'organization' client scope (realm-config.json L1156-1183) contributes exactly one mapper — oidc-organization-membership-mapper (L1166-1181) — with access.token.claim=true, id.token.claim=true, introspection.token.claim=true, multivalued=true, jsonType.label=String, claim.name=organization. addOrganizationId and addOrganizationAttributes are unset, locking the OOTB array-of-strings shape (organizations.md §1).
reasoning.step_3_access_token_member: initToken sets the access-token base claims (id, typ, iat, azp, iss, scope=getScopeString(), acr, sid, exp; sub NOT set here per invariant 1 since the session is persistent for password grant). scope claim = names of allowed scopes with isIncludeInTokenScope()=true: profile (true L745), web-origins (false L979), acr (false L1081), roles (false L1106), organization (true L1160), basic (false L1283), email (true L1233). After client-filter (DCSC.L200) and the true-only filter, we have {profile, organization, email}. attachOIDCScope prepends openid (the request param is openid-bearing). Final scope claim contents (set): {openid, profile, organization, email}. (organizations.md §3.1 documents a side-finding that 'organization' may appear TWICE in the literal scope string for single-member users — but the prediction-target asks for the SET, which de-duplicates.) The oidc-organization-membership-mapper then fires with access.token.claim=true; user has exactly one membership (acme); §3.1 single-membership lucky-path emits the claim. Wire value: ['acme'].
reasoning.step_4_id_token_member: generateIDToken seeds an empty IDToken with the 11 explicitly-listed fields (base-claims.md L92-104). scope is NOT one of them. transformIDToken then runs the OIDCIDTokenMapper-side dispatch over the same mapper set, gated by id.token.claim. The oidc-organization-membership-mapper has id.token.claim=true (realm-config.json L1171), so it fires; same setClaim logic → ['acme']. No mapper in this fixture writes a 'scope' claim to the ID token. Therefore: organization=['acme'] (shape 4), scope=absent.
reasoning.step_5_nonmember_divergence: Non-member: scope resolution and mapper-set assembly are IDENTICAL to the member (same client, same scope param, same set of attached default scopes; the user's role mappings don't gate scope inclusion here because no relevant scope carries role mappings that fail for adv4-nonmember). scope claim is therefore identical: {openid, profile, organization, email} on the access token, absent on the ID token. The single point of divergence is inside the oidc-organization-membership-mapper's setClaim: §3.1 says zero-membership → null write → invariant 11 (NON_NULL) drops the claim from the wire. Both access and ID surfaces drop it (same mapper, both toggles true, both have null source). organization claim: shape 1 (absent) on both surfaces. Empirical anchor in §2 directly cites adversarial-4/actual-token-nonmember.json as having no organization key (this is a forward-pointer in the docs; I have NOT read that file).
reasoning.step_6_post_mapper: restrictRequestedAudience (invariant 8): REQUESTED_AUDIENCE_CLIENTS is not set (no token-exchange / requested-audience refresh in either request). No-op. sid-nulling (invariant 12): password grant retains sid (jti prefix 'onrtcc:' for password persistent-session per fixtures), but this doesn't touch the organization claim. No post-mapper transform alters either commitment.
